title: Data Status Report
text: Data Status Report provides overview quality, completeness, readiness camera-trap dataset generating final Ecological Report. helps users check whether main input files, metadata fields, deployment information, observation records, taxonomy, timestamps, annotation information, spatial data complete internally consistent. report especially useful first quality-control step. allows users identify missing values, duplicated records, invalid timestamps, incomplete metadata, spatial issues, inconsistencies deployments observations. Based checks, users can decide whether dataset ready reporting whether correction needed ecological analyses performed. Figure 1 summarises camtrapReport checks readiness camera-trap dataset ecological reporting. data loaded camData(), status() function runs automated checks main input files, metadata, deployments, observations, timestamps, taxonomy, spatial information, annotation records. output helps users identify potential issues decide whether dataset ready generating final Ecological Report. Figure 1. Workflow generating Data Status Report camera-trap data using camtrapReport. example, species table can inspected check species detected many captures recorded species. Together, status(cm, view = TRUE) cm$data_status provide human-readable HTML report direct access underlying data-quality summaries R. makes Data Status Report useful documenting data readiness, identifying issues, improving dataset generating final Ecological Report.
code:
cm <- camData( data = "/path/camera-trap-data.zip", habitat = "/path/habitat.csv", study_area = "/path/study_area.shp") status(cm, filename = "/path/outputs/status", view = TRUE) When `view = TRUE`, the generated report is opened in the browser. This provides a quick, human-readable overview of dataset quality, completeness, and consistency. An existing file with the same name may be replaced. Use a deliberate, versioned filename when reports from multiple processing runs must be retained.
## Example Data Status Reports Below are previews of Data Status Reports generated with `camtrapReport` for different camera-trap monitoring projects. These examples illustrate the presentation of dataset completeness and potential issues. Click a preview to open the corresponding complete report. Reports can also be generated locally from a Camtrap DP dataset using the workflow described above.

## Exploring data-status results in R The results of the data-status checks are also stored inside the `camReport` object. Users can explore these results directly in R through `cm$data_status`. This is useful when users want to inspect the underlying tables, extract summaries, or use the quality-control outputs in another workflow. ``` r # Explore all data-status outputs stored in the camReport object cm$data_status # Show the available data-status components names(cm$data_status) cm$data_status$Spatial cm$data_status$Temporal cm$data_status$Essentials cm$data_status$Annotation cm$data_status$Validation cm$data_status$Species cm$data_status$Visuals # View species summary table cm$data_status$Species$Table

title: Manage report modules — modules
code: # List modules as a hierarchical tree module_tree <- list_Modules() head(module_tree) #>              ID         name  parent level          label #> introduction  1 introduction   .root     0 - introduction #> methods       2      methods   .root     0      - methods #> study_area    3   study_area methods     1   - study_area #> sampling      4     sampling methods     1     - sampling #> location      5     location methods     1     - location #> effort        6       effort methods     1       - effort  # List modules in table form module_table <- list_Modules(tree = FALSE) head(module_table) #>   ID         name  parent valid status #> 1  1 introduction   .root  TRUE     ok #> 2  2      methods   .root  TRUE     ok #> 3  3   study_area methods  TRUE     ok #> 4  4     sampling methods  TRUE     ok #> 5  5     location methods  TRUE     ok #> 6  6       effort methods  TRUE     ok  if (interactive()) {   # Mutating operations require an explicit writable module directory.   module_dir <- tempfile("camtrapReport-modules-")   dir.create(module_dir)    bundled_dir <- system.file("reportSections", package = "camtrapReport")   files <- list.files(bundled_dir, full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)   file.copy(files, module_dir, recursive = TRUE)    # Example:   # add_Module("new_module.yml", after = "captures", dir = module_dir) }

code: example_dataset <- system.file(   "external",   "dataset",   package = "camtrapReport" )  cm <- camData(example_dataset)  # Use one lightweight section for the ecological report cm <- sections(cm, "introduction") #>  #> The report sections are updated.  # Generate an ecological report in a temporary directory report_stem <- tempfile("camtrapReport-report-") report_file <- report(   cm,   filename = report_stem,   view = FALSE ) #> Rendering R Markdown report ... #> Report generated at: C:\Users\ebrah010\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmp4YV1ap\camtrapReport-report-1c48109949.html  file.exists(report_file) #> [1] TRUE  # Generate a data-status report in a temporary directory status_stem <- tempfile("camtrapReport-status-") status_file <- status(   cm,   filename = status_stem,   view = FALSE ) #> Rendering R Markdown data_status report ... #> Data_Status Report generated at: C:\Users\ebrah010\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmp4YV1ap\camtrapReport-status-1c4819393485.html  file.exists(status_file) #> [1] TRUE  # Remove files generated by the examples unlink(c(   report_file,   paste0(report_stem, ".Rmd"),   status_file,   paste0(status_stem, ".Rmd") ))
